newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks seen sound despite returns drop.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks seen sound despite returns drop.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Wednesday that the Philippine banking system is still "sound and strong" despite the declining return on equity (ROE) in the sector due to stiff competition.
"The average return on equity ... has been going down from a high of 28 percent. In 1995, it was less than 14 percent," Singson told a private television channel.
He, however, said that this should not be a cause for alarm since the country's biggest banks were still posting 20 percent ROE last year.
"The banking system is sound and strong," he said, adding that there would be more banks operating this year even if the industry has more than 50 already.
The banking system has been refocusing its strategy following the entry of 10 new foreign banks in the past two years as well as an pending hike in minimum capital requirements.
Singson further said he had asked the Congress to allow more foreign banks to set up branches in the country since the first ten banks have been performing very well.
"So far, yes, yes," Singson said when asked whether he was satisfied with the performance of the new foreign banks.

"Our main purpose in allowing foreign banks to establish a branch for the first time in 50 years has been accomplished -- that is to promote trade and investment in this country," he added. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
